title: Seagrass meadow loss and restoration
bottleneck: Seagrass meadows bury carbon 35 times faster than tropical forests per area, yet they are disappearing from coastal development, poor water quality, and warming — and restoration is painfully slow because seeds are hard to collect, seedlings wash away, and water quality must improve first. Globally, restoration covers a negligible fraction of losses, and many meadows that die from heat stress cannot re-establish in the warmer water.
why_it_blocks: Seagrass loss removes nursery habitat for a fifth of the world's largest fisheries plus coastal protection and carbon burial. The restoration bottleneck means the decline is effectively one-way in most regions.
current_state: Mechanized seed planting and sediment restoration have improved success rates in places like Virginia's coastal bays, one of the few large-scale wins. But these remain exceptions; the default trajectory worldwide is continued loss.
